observations.explanation: On M3ToolEval, CodeAct has the highest success rate for 12 of 17 models and uses fewer average turns for 12 of 17. The results include especially strong gains for several closed-source models, though not all (PDF pp. 5).
The paper reports 7,139 CodeActInstruct trajectories and evaluates CodeActAgent on agent tasks as well as general tasks such as MMLU, HumanEval, GSM8K, and MT-Bench (PDF pp. 8–9).

The paper states that M3ToolEval contains 82 human-curated instances across several domains (PDF p. 5). Treating the benchmark’s coverage and stability as uncertain is a qualified limitation, not a claim that the paper demonstrated a defect.

The results are not uniform: for example, claude-instant-1 performs better with JSON than CodeAct on M3ToolEval, while some API-Bank results also favor JSON or text. The paper’s overall format advantage is therefore conditional (PDF pp. 5–6).
